newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel vows to press ahead with Jewish settlement.
newsitem.headline: Israel vows to press ahead with Jewish settlement.

text.p: Israel vowed on Thursday it would break ground soon on a widely criticised Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem but said it was reconsidering orders to close four Palestinian offices in the city.

"I say in the name of the prime minister there won't be any delays in the building of Har Homa," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak told Israeli army radio in a reference to the settlement.
"At the beginning of next week, apparently, those bulldozers will arrive and they will start to build there as the state of Israel has decided and will do," he said.

Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said Israel was reconsidering its closure orders after Palestinian officials promised in writing that the four offices had no connection to PLO leader Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority.
"We must examine this thing," Kahalani told army radio. "It could be my purpose was achieved."
"They claim in their declaration...that they will have no link whatsoever in the future with the Palestinian Authority and in fact such a declaration was never before given," Kahalani said.
Netanyahu summoned his inner security cabinet to discuss the issues which have prompted Arafat to call an emergency meeting of international envoys in self-ruled Gaza for Saturday.

Israel views Jerusalem as its undivided capital while the PLO regards East Jerusalem, captured by the Jewish state in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed, as the capital of a future Palestinian state.

Netanyahu angered Palestinians and drew international condemnation with a cabinet decision this month to build 6,500 houses for Jews on the hilltop Israel calls Har Homa and Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim.

Palestinians were further enraged when Israeli police issued closure orders to four Palestinian offices in East Jerusalem, saying they were run by the Palestinian Authority in violation of Israeli-PLO peace deals.

Palestinians deny the offices are linked to the Palestinian Authority, insisting that the closure orders were part of an Israeli intimidation campaign. The status of Jerusalem is up for negotiation at final peace talks due to begin next week.
